transcript.text: f/f freezer keeps icing up bottom drawer wont shut proper, defrosted it 2wks ago already full of ice again. indesit

Since the ice came back so quickly after you defrosted it, this points to a fault with the automatic defrost system rather than just user error. The most common cause is that the heater or thermostat has failed, meaning the machine isn't melting the frost during its cycle. To tell me exactly which part might be faulty, I need the model number. It’s usually on a sticker inside the fridge (often near the salad drawer) or on the door frame. What does it say?
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its IB55532W, read it off the rating plate. its a static freezer tho, no auto defrost, manual defrost one

Thanks for clarifying that. Since it's a static manual-defrost model, the ice isn't caused by a failed automatic heater; instead, moisture is getting inside from somewhere else. The most common cause of rapid re-icing in these units is warm air entering through a faulty door seal (gasket). Please switch the fridge off and unplug it to clear the ice completely. Once it's defrosted, please check the rubber door seal carefully: is it torn, brittle, or has any part of it come away from the door frame? Also, when the door is closed with a piece of paper in the gap, does it grip tightly?
ok did the seal check. bottom corner of the freezer door seal is split about 5cm and the hinge-side bottom bit is flattened. paper slides straight out at that corner, grips everywhere else

[Heading: Likely cause: door seal]
That split and flattened section of the seal is most likely letting warm air in, which explains why the ice has built up again so quickly. You will need to replace that freezer door seal (gasket). As I couldn't find a confirmed match for model IB55532W in my parts database, please contact Indesit customer support or check their official website with your model number to order the correct part. Once you have it, fitting is usually straightforward: pull off the old seal and press the new one into place.
